title: Unique Index
description: Learn how to use unique indexes to enforce uniqueness of values in one or more columns.

data.text: A unique index ensures the index key columns do not contain any duplicate values. If a unique index has one column, values in that column will be unique. If it has multiple columns, the combination of values must be unique.

data.title: Basic UNIQUE INDEX syntax
data.content: Creates a unique index on a single column.
data.code:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX index_name
ON table_name(column_list);

data.text: You can create a unique index on the email column to ensure no duplicate emails exist:

data.title: Unique index on email
data.content: Creates a unique index for the email column.
data.code:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ix_cust_email
ON sales.customers(email);

data.text: SQL Server treats NULL values the same in a unique index. If you create a unique index on a nullable column, you can have only one NULL value in that column.
Both unique index and UNIQUE constraint enforce uniqueness. When you create a unique constraint, SQL Server creates a unique index behind the scenes.

data.title: Unique Index Key Points
points: A unique index enforces that index key values are not duplicated.
Unique indexes can be clustered or non-clustered.
Only one NULL value is allowed per column in a unique index.
A unique constraint creates a unique index automatically.
